prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of GLP-1 and of its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on B045 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 showed that all six of us reach it by the same scientific route, not by counting opening ballots. That route runs from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect (Holst, Drucker) through identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov) to receptor pharmacology and drugs with large randomized effects on glycemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The mechanism has been independently confirmed for about three decades, so maturity is not in question. I also considered whether a second part is needed. It is not: B045 is a complete achievement on its own, and adding a second part under the three-person cap would mean cutting a B045 name or crediting a second field with one or two people just to fill the space. The Committee has no obligation to award two parts.
statement.case_against: The weak point is still attribution, and round 1 did not remove it. Habener is not among the credited names, nobody has audited the Mojsov, Habener and Holst priority record, and the cap leaves out Knudsen, whose acylated analogues are what patients actually receive. I am choosing Mojsov over Knudsen on the principle that the Committee rewards the discovery that opened the field and that analogue design rests on knowing the active peptide. That principle is a judgment, not a finding, and it would be wrong to present it as settled. A prize read as honouring the hormone while skipping the drug could look incomplete, and the commercial scale of semaglutide and liraglutide should not be mistaken for scientific priority either way.

responses.point: She proposes the same trio but says leaving out Knudsen is uncomfortable, and suggests the citation wording could address the analogue step.
responses.response: I accept the discomfort and would handle it the way she suggests, in the wording and not by adding a name. My citation says the active form made possible incretin-based therapies, which acknowledges the development step without implying a fourth laureate. I would not go further and name analogues or long-acting drugs in the citation, because that would turn it into a development prize and would sharpen the question of why Knudsen is absent. Where I correct my own round 1: I described her as proposing Knudsen in the trio. She did not. Her file lists Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, so we agree on the names and differ only in how uneasy the Knudsen exclusion makes us.

responses.point: He now accepts that colleagues weigh GLP-1's maturity more heavily than he did, but keeps the unfolded protein response as his own first choice and as his preferred fallback.
responses.response: I take his point that the UPR is the cleanest mechanism on the list, and I agree Walter and Mori is a tidy two-person credit. His own uncertainty about PERK and ATF6 is also mine, since a prize for the pathway that leaves out Ron, Kaufman and the other arms invites the completeness objection. I do not think the UPR is ahead of B045 this year, because its link to disease is still mostly correlative. I keep it as my first alternative and will say plainly that I would support it in a later year if disease-relevant evidence matures, for example from targeted modulation of the pathway in patients.

responses.point: As chair he lists Drucker, Holst and Mojsov as the scientific discovery core and admits that his recollection of the priority history is unverified.
responses.response: The chair's candour about the priority record applies to me as well, and the chair summary is right that none of us has audited it. I will not claim to have resolved it. What I can say is that the three roles are distinct and each is independently documented in the supplied evidence: physiology of the native hormone, biology of proglucagon-derived peptides and translation, and the active truncated peptide. If the Committee is going to rely on Mojsov's role, someone should check the actual record before the ballot. I do not think uncertainty about Habener justifies replacing Mojsov with Knudsen, because that swap rests on a different principle and not on better evidence.

responses.point: He asks whether a split prize between GLP-1 and CAR-T is feasible within three people without sacrificing credit in one part.
responses.response: I do not think it is. A split would give GLP-1 one or two names, and any pair drawn from Drucker, Holst and Mojsov removes a person whose contribution is essential to the chain. It would also leave CAR-T with the June and Sadelain pair that I already consider more fragile than the three-name version, because Rosenberg's TIL and adoptive-transfer work is adjacent to CAR design and Eshhar is not credited. Neither part would be well credited. I would keep B016 as an alternative and not force a two-part configuration that weakens both.

responses.point: He worries that some of the clinical weight of GLP-1 sits in industrial development, which the Committee has historically credited cautiously, and that safety and durability are still being characterised.
responses.response: I agree with both parts, and they support our trio. Because so much of the clinical weight sits in industrial development, the credit should go to the academic discoveries that made the drugs possible. On long-term safety, the question is whether the discovery has held up, and by that measure it has: the physiology and the receptor biology have been confirmed repeatedly, and ongoing characterisation of the drugs does not undermine the finding. I would still want the citation to say what the discovery made possible and stop short of endorsing any specific product.

uncertainties: Priority among Mojsov, Habener and Holst for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide has not been audited by any member and remains unresolved on the supplied evidence; Habener is outside the credited names.
Whether the Committee will accept the discovery-over-development principle that puts Mojsov ahead of Knudsen for the third place, or will treat that as arbitrary.
Whether B007 will gain enough disease-relevant evidence, and whether the omission of PERK, ATF6, Ron and Kaufman is acceptable, to stand as a first alternative in a later year.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I have co-authored with colleagues on this Committee (Linnarsson, Frisén), but no shortlisted credited name is among my documented collaborators, and shared KI affiliation alone does not establish a tie. I request no recusal and have nothing to update from round 1.
